title: Cap. V Obj. 4: if predestination without foresight of faith, then save without satisfaction of justice
latin: Obj. 4. Si Deus praedestinaret quosdam ad vitam absque intuitu fidei antecedaneae, tum tales etiam servare vellet absque justitiae suae satisfactione; cum etiam tales magis diligeret, quam propriam suam justitiam: At haec falsa sunt: Ergo et illud unde consequuntur, scilicet, Deum praedestinare quenquam ante praevisionem fidei, quae satisfactionem Christi particularibus personis applicat ad salutem.
pass_a: Objection 4. If God were to predestinate certain ones to life without an intuition of antecedent faith, then he would also will to save such without satisfaction of his justice; since he would also love such more than his own proper justice: But these things are false: Therefore also that from which they follow, namely, that God predestinates anyone before foresight of faith, which applies the satisfaction of Christ to particular persons unto salvation.
pass_b: Obj. 4. If God predestinated some to life without intuition of antecedent faith, then he would also will to save them without satisfaction of his justice — loving them more than his own justice. But those are false. Therefore so is what follows from them: that God predestinates anyone before foresight of faith, which applies Christ's satisfaction to particular persons unto salvation.

title: Cap. V Obj. 4 Sol: eternal will to save ≠ all that concurs in the consummated external act
latin: Sol. Respondeo, Non concurrere ad voluntatem aeternam servandi in arcano electionis proposito inclusam, illa omnia quae concurrunt ad voluntatem servandi in ipso actu externo consummatam. Negamus igitur Majoris consequentiam, atque dicimus, Deum nunquam habuisse voluntatem servandi quenquam absque satisfactione justitiae suae; habuisse tamen voluntatem dandi quosdam Christo, dandi illis fidem per quam unio haec fieret, et per quam mediante hac fide Deo pro illis per Christi mortem efficaciter satisfaceret: atque haec omnia antecedenter ad praevisionem fidei ut in illis certe et infallibiliter existentis; non tamen absque praevisione, aut excludendo praevisionem fidei illis ex gratia Dei infallibiliter impertiendae.
pass_a: Solution. I answer, That not all those things concur unto the eternal will of saving enclosed in the secret purpose of election, which concur unto the will of saving consummated in the very external act. We therefore deny the consequence of the Major, and say that God never had a will of saving anyone without satisfaction of his justice; yet had a will of giving certain ones to Christ, of giving them faith by which this union would be made, and by which, with this faith mediating, he would efficaciously be satisfied for them through the death of Christ: and all these things antecedently to the foresight of faith as certainly and infallibly existing in them; yet not without foresight, or by excluding the foresight of faith to be infallibly imparted to them from the grace of God.
pass_b: Sol. I answer: not everything that concurs in the will to save as consummated in the external act also concurs in the eternal will to save enclosed in election's secret purpose. We deny the Major's consequence. God never had a will to save anyone without satisfaction of his justice; yet he had a will to give certain ones to Christ, to give them faith by which that union would be made, and by which, with that faith mediating, he would be efficaciously satisfied for them through Christ's death — all of this antecedent to foresight of faith as already certainly and infallibly existing in them, yet not without foresight, nor by excluding foresight of faith to be infallibly imparted to them from God's grace.

lemmas.gloss: give some to Christ and faith

title: Cap. V Obj. 4 Sol close: they deduce from foresight denied secundum quid, not simply excluded
latin: Fallere igitur nos conantur hujusmodi argumentationibus, dum illa absurda quae recte deducantur ab exclusa aut simpliciter negata praevisione fidei, illi deducunt a negata praevisione fidei secundum quid, hoc est, ut antecedanea conditione ad ipsam praedestinationem.
pass_a: They therefore try to deceive us by arguments of this kind, while those absurdities which are rightly deduced from foresight of faith excluded or simply denied, they deduce from foresight of faith denied in a certain respect, that is, as an antecedent condition unto predestination itself.
pass_b: So they try to deceive us with such arguments: absurdities that follow only if foresight of faith is excluded or simply denied, they deduce from foresight denied secundum quid — that is, denied as an antecedent condition of predestination itself.
